keyVerseText: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb אָחַר (ʼâchar) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the idea of remaining behind or delaying. Its core sense involves a temporal or spatial lag—either to tarry longer in a place or to defer an action. This root meaning goes beyond the simple English glosses of delay or hinder, as it encompasses an intentional or unintentional hesitation that affects progress or movement, reflecting both physical and metaphorical postponement.
usageInScripture: Across its 17 occurrences, אָחַר consistently appears with meanings related to delay, tarrying, or hindrance. The top translations include 'make no tarrying,' 'defer,' and 'hinder me,' indicating a semantic range from passive remaining behind to active causing of delay. This variety shows that the verb can describe both the subject's own hesitation and an external force that impedes action, revealing a nuanced understanding of time and movement in the biblical context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אָחַר enriches our grasp of biblical patience, obedience, and divine timing. The word's original sense of delay or hesitation highlights human tendencies to procrastinate or remain behind, contrasting with the call to swift obedience and faithfulness. Theologically, this verb reminds believers that God's purposes move forward without unnecessary delay, and that hindering or deferring God's work can be spiritually detrimental. It encourages trust in God's timing and the avoidance of slackness in following His commands, aligning with the biblical exhortation to diligence and faithfulness in the Christian life.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 24:56, the phrase 'Hinder me not' directly uses the concept of אָחַר to express a plea against delay or obstruction. The speaker acknowledges God's blessing on his journey and requests that he not be caused to tarry but be allowed to proceed promptly to his master. This use of the word emphasizes the urgency and divine endorsement of the mission, illustrating how delay can impede God-ordained plans and highlighting the importance of timely obedience in fulfilling God's purposes.
